text:
alex: Planning to land RBAC change that tightens the console role matrix: viewer->read-only, editor->edit, admin unchanged. Need a quick security review before we flip the UI gating and backend checks. main concerns: implicit elevation paths, audit logging for role changes, and KMS metadata on exported audit blobs.
maria: +1. Where are we storing role-change events today? do we have KMS key id in the blob?
sam: role-change events go to audit-events topic, payload currently looks like: 
```json
{
  "user": "alice",
  "action": "assign_role",
  "target": "project:123",
  "role": "editor",
  "meta": {}
}
```
no KMS info now.
chris: Risk: API still accepts legacy role aliases (eg "project_editor"), that mapping is done in auth-service. If we tighten UI only, API clients could bypass and get elevated perms. we should block legacy alias resolution or enforce server-side mapping.
jen: Product question: do we want the console to show explicit "read-only" label for viewer? it's confusing to customers if UI and API labels differ.
leah: propose a rollout plan w/ feature flag + canary: enable enforcement in auth-service behind ff-2025-rbac, enable ui labels after 10% canary for 24h. Also add a migration job that rewrites alias assignments to canonical roles.
jordan: I can own the migration job. quick question: if we rewrite historical audit events, we must not lose original alias. attach both alias + canonical to the event.
alex: agree — audit must be append-only. keep original_alias and canonical_role in event. add kms_key_id when exporting to long-term storage.
sam: implement audit log patch: 
```json
{
  "user": "alice",
  "action": "assign_role",
  "target": "project:123",
  "role_alias": "project_editor",
  "canonical_role": "editor",
  "actor_ip": "1.2.3.4",
  "kms_key_id": "projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/audit/cryptoKeys/arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd"
}
```
chris: also add a boolean "via_ui" flag so we can differentiate API vs console changes for triage.
maria: agree. For incident response, needing to filter by kms_key_id will help trace who exported logs.
jen: on UX, will add copy: "Viewer (read-only) — cannot modify resources or change settings". hoping that reduces support tickets.
leah: ops question: can we avoid rewriting audit-events topic? maybe emit a mapping-event stream instead and have consumers join to resolve alias -> canonical for history. less risky.
jordan: that's safer. migration job becomes optional cleanup. I'll implement the mapping stream and a small consumer for analytics.
sec-bot: Security checklist: 1) block legacy alias resolution in auth-service when ff is on; 2) add kms_key_id to exported blobs; 3) emit mapping_event stream; 4) add alert if role-change occurs without actor_ip.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for auth-service patch to staging at 2025-04-18T15:00Z, canary rollout next day.
alex: action items: jordan -> mapping stream + consumer (owner), sam -> audit payload change + via_ui flag, leah -> feature flag config + canary plan, chris -> block legacy alias resolution PR, jen -> UX copy. We'll sync tomorrow 10am.
maria: thanks — I will run a quick vuln triage to ensure no privilege-escalation paths remain, will post findings in this thread. :mag: 
alex: thanks all. tagging @sec-bot to start a short walkthrough doc once patch lands.
